newsitem.title: JAPAN: INTERVIEW - Canon eyes Y4 trln group sales in 2000.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Canon eyes Y4 trln group sales in 2000.

text.p: Canon Inc says it should be able to expand its group sales to four trillion yen in calendar 2000 if the yen does not surge back to around 110 yen to the dollar.
Canon president Fujio Mitarai told Reuters that group sales would likely expand to 2.8 trillion yen this calendar year.
"Our target is to expand our group sales to four trillion yen in 2000. Unless the yen strengthens to below 110 yen to the dollar, I think this target is attainable," he said in a recent interview.
Canon is scheduled to to unveil its group business results for 1996 on Wednesday.
The performance is expected to be as good as the firm"s parent results announced last week, showing it posted record growth in current profits for a second consecutive year, a company spokesman said.
Mitarai also said Canon will focus on developing its new business of making key components for high-tech industry.
"Our company"s next stage of growth will be based on the business of making high-tech components, such as display panels and silicon wafers," he said.

He predicted that by next year a breakthrough in production technology for Canon"s ferroelectric liquid crystal display -- which was introduced to the market in May 1995 -- would make the product economically viable.

He also said some Canon group firms will seek to upgrade their share listings -- either from the second section to the first section of the Tokyo Stock Exchange or from the over-the-counter market to the second section -- by the end of 1998.
Such firms include Canon Electronics Inc, now listed on the second section, and Canon Aptex Inc and Canon Components Inc, registered on the over-the-counter market.
On currencies, Mitarai said the dollar may trade at around 120 yen for the time being, because the import-oriented U.S. economy relies heavily on a firm dollar.
A weaker yen helps boost sales of exports. About 80 percent of Canon"s revenues come from exports.
On Canon"s recent decision to pull out of the personal computer business, Mitarai said it is only taking a temporary break as the business is not profitable at present.

The company said last month that it would transfer the running of its personal computer operations to its subsidiary Canon Sales Co Inc and sell its 20 percent stake in NeXT Software Inc of the United States, which is being acquired by Apple Computer Inc.
He nevertheless pointed out that it is becoming increasingly important that printers, the company"s prime revenue source, are compatible with a de facto standard for computer networks.
